extraction.Name: Susan Valandry
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent to her 320 acre allotment; but that she was told that it was necessary for her to take it, so she did
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold 80 acres of her allotment to A.S. White, of Kadoka, South Dakota, for $500.00; then turned the land over to him (the banker of Kadoka), it being 240 acres
extraction.Buyer: 80 acres sold to A.S. White of Kadoka, South Dakota for $500.00; 240 acres turned over to the banker of Kadoka, South Dakota
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: got almost entirely behind with her taxes; then, in 1925, she sold 80 acres of her allotment to A.S. White, of Kadoka, South Dakota, for $500.00, then she paid up her taxes
extraction.Occupation/Income: she and her four children are supported by her husband, Vetal Valandry; and her husband is a farmer
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent; health is not good, having suffered a paralytic stroke and was in the hospital over a year; has four minor children whose health is good; supported by husband Vetal Valandry, a farmer; son George Brown owed the bank at Kadoka and she went his security; son-in-law Frank Baumann urged her to put land in his name to protect herself; banker of Kadoka told her and her son George Brown that he intended to either have her land or her stock; she never received any help from the County or Government; document dated November 17, 1928
